payload.title: [sfu-media-3] SFU transports leaked on leave and on every re-join — unbounded growth / DoS
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING sfu-media-3 (high/resource-leak, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/calls/call-control-plane.ts
LINES: 343-399, 526-562

WHAT: Each joinCall() calls issueJoinToken(), which unconditionally createWebRtcTransport twice (send+recv) on the call's router (sfu-media-plane.ts:185-194). leaveCall() (lines 526-562) marks the participant 'left' and emits an event but never closes those transports — the only teardown is releaseSession→closeRouter at full call end (sfu-media-plane.ts:216-221). joinCall has no already-joined guard, so a participant can repeatedly join (or rejoin after leaving) and each call mints a fresh send+recv transport pair that is never reclaimed until the whole call ends. The backend tracks transports unbounded in RouterEntry.transports (mediasoup-sfu-backend.ts:108-113). The fake test even asserts transportCount grows to 2 per issue with no per-participant dedup (sfu-media-plane.test.ts:106-107).

IMPACT: A single authenticated participant can drive unbounded server-side WebRTC transport allocation on a long-lived call by repeatedly join/leave, exhausting the mediasoup worker's RTC port range (rtcMin..rtcMax, default 40000-49999 → ~10k ports) and memory — a per-call resource-exhaustion DoS that degrades or kills the SFU for everyone on that node. Even normal churn (reconnects) steadily leaks ports for the call's lifetime.

SUGGESTED FIX: On leaveCall, close the participant's send+recv transports (closeTransport) and their producers/consumers. Make issueJoinToken idempotent per (callId,userId,deviceId): reuse/replace existing transports for a rejoining participant rather than minting new ones. Add per-call and per-participant transport caps.
